mt_red_lodge.blurb: Red Lodge climbing is based around the town of Red Lodge in south-central Montana. It is overwhelmingly sport, with a few trad lines, and the grades lean hard: most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.13, with only a thin set of easier ones. The Palace and Headstrong Buttress both sit at around 7,000 feet or a little above. The Palace is reached by a steep trail of 10 to 30 minutes and its aspects give both sun and shade, while Headstrong Buttress mixes crack and face climbing, mostly in one pitch, after a hike of about 15 minutes straight up. Nippinino, Red Lodge Creek and Confluence Crag also hold plenty of climbs.

nh_dumplingtown_hill_the_dump.blurb: Dumplingtown Hill, known as The Dump, is in Candia in the Merrimack Valley of southern New Hampshire. It is mainly a boulder and trad area, with a few top-rope lines and no bolted sport routes. Problems and routes stand roughly 12 to 50 feet tall. Boulder grades run mostly from V0 to V3, with a few much harder lines, and the roped climbs span 5.5 to 5.12. The crag faces the sun and dries fairly quickly: boulders dry fastest, while low-angle slabs take longer because of groundwater seepage. Dumplingtown Hill South and Dumplingtown Hill North hold the most climbs, with The Left End and Krazy Krags among the boulder areas.

or_v_monument_area.blurb: The Monument Area is a group of towers and formations within Smith Rock in Central Oregon. Sport climbing dominates, with a smaller amount of trad. Most routes sit between 5.10 and 5.13, with 5.11 and 5.12 the most common and only a few easier lines. Recent development has added single-pitch sport routes, mostly 5.11 to 5.12, at the base of several formations. The area is called a prime fall and early winter destination at Smith. Anglin's Buttress is a southwest-facing wall about 350 feet tall with multi-pitch sport routes, and the area also holds The Monument, Big Ben Tower, Puddy's Tower and Victoria Tower.

pa_mcconnells_mill_state_park.blurb: McConnells Mill State Park is a small park in western Pennsylvania with two climbing and rappelling areas. The rock is sandstone, and the climbing is mostly bouldering and top-roping, with some trad lines; some cliffs have bolt anchors while others use slung trees. Boulder problems run from V0 to about V5, and roped climbs span a broad range from 5.4 to 5.12, mostly in the middle grades. Rim Road Climbing Area holds the most climbs and sits across the creek from the old mill. North Country Trail Area is all boulder problems, and Breakneck Bridge is the more advanced and rugged of the two roped areas.

tn_denny_east.blurb: Denny East is one side of Denny Cove, about half an hour from Chattanooga and just north of Jasper, Tennessee. The cove's cliffs are multi-colored sandstone, with terrain that ranges from long overhanging walls and big roofs to slabs, cracks and corners. Denny East itself is almost entirely sport climbing, with a couple of trad lines. Grades are concentrated in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with a decent number of 5.10s and a few 5.13s. Buffet Wall holds the most climbs by a wide margin, followed by Ladies Delight, Pig Wall and Four Horsemen.

tx_continental_ranch.blurb: Continental Ranch is in West Texas along the Pecos River, where the river has cut roughly 17 miles of steep limestone canyons through semi-arid hills. The climbing is almost entirely sport, with a few trad routes. Grades mostly run from 5.9 to 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common and a small number of 5.13s. Shumla Bend holds the most climbs, followed by Weir Dam. The Weir Dam walls face south and take full sun all day, with no real shade in that part of the canyon, and its climbing leans toward thin, technical slabs along with aretes, corners and roofs.
